verdict: AppLovin grew revenue 66% to $1.66B and kept two-thirds of it as profit — net income jumped 84% to $1.10B as its AXON ad platform kept compounding.

segments.name: Advertising platform
segments.note: Ads placed through AppLovin's AXON platform — advertisers pay to reach users inside other companies' apps, and AXON's AI decides which ads to show. AppLovin sold its own apps business in 2025, so this platform is the whole company.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building and improving the AXON ad platform — down 22% YoY after the apps-business sale shrank the company.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to advertisers and app publishers — down 21% YoY.

takeaways.title: Growth stayed hot
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 66% to $1.66B — a year ago the same platform did $999M in the quarter — as advertisers kept shifting budgets to AXON.

takeaways.title: Two-thirds kept as profit
takeaways.text: Net income of $1.10B is 66% of revenue, up 84% in a year — an almost unheard-of margin for an ad business, because software costs almost nothing extra to deliver.

takeaways.title: Cash in, buybacks out
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $1.31B in a single quarter, and AppLovin spent $482M buying back its own shares — $2.58B over the full year.

otherDetail: Interest expense and a loss on settling debt cost $51M, partly offset by $29M of other income — a net $22M expense.
footerNote: AppLovin reports as a single segment. Its former apps business was sold in 2025 and appears as discontinued operations in earlier periods; there were none this quarter.
